@REM OrcaSlicer build script for Windows with VS auto-detect
@echo off
set WP=%CD%
set _START_TIME=%TIME%

@REM Default target architecture to the host CPU arch; override by passing
@REM "x64" or "arm64" as an argument. PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432 covers a 32-bit
@REM shell running on a 64-bit OS, where PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE reads "x86".
set arch=x64
if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%"=="ARM64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432%"=="ARM64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%1"=="arm64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%2"=="arm64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%1"=="x64" set arch=x64
if /I "%2"=="x64" set arch=x64

@REM Check for Ninja Multi-Config option (-x)
set USE_NINJA=0
for %%a in (%*) do (
    if "%%a"=="-x" set USE_NINJA=1
)

if "%USE_NINJA%"=="1" (
    echo Using Ninja Multi-Config generator
    set CMAKE_GENERATOR="Ninja Multi-Config"
    set VS_VERSION=Ninja
    goto :generator_ready
)

@REM Detect Visual Studio version using msbuild
echo Detecting Visual Studio version using msbuild...

@REM Try to get MSBuild version - the output format varies by VS version
set VS_MAJOR=
for /f "tokens=*" %%i in ('msbuild -version 2^>^&1 ^| findstr /r "^[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*"') do (
    for /f "tokens=1 delims=." %%a in ("%%i") do set VS_MAJOR=%%a
    set MSBUILD_OUTPUT=%%i
    goto :version_found
)

@REM Alternative method for newer MSBuild versions
if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="" (
    for /f "tokens=*" %%i in ('msbuild -version 2^>^&1 ^| findstr /r "[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*"') do (
        for /f "tokens=1 delims=." %%a in ("%%i") do set VS_MAJOR=%%a
        set MSBUILD_OUTPUT=%%i
        goto :version_found
    )
)

:version_found
echo MSBuild version detected: %MSBUILD_OUTPUT%
echo Major version: %VS_MAJOR%

if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="" (
    echo Error: Could not determine Visual Studio version from msbuild
    echo Please ensure Visual Studio and MSBuild are properly installed
    exit /b 1
)

if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="16" (
    set VS_VERSION=2019
    set CMAKE_GENERATOR="Visual Studio 16 2019"
) else if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="17" (
    set VS_VERSION=2022
    set CMAKE_GENERATOR="Visual Studio 17 2022"
) else if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="18" (
    set VS_VERSION=2026
    set CMAKE_GENERATOR="Visual Studio 18 2026"
) else (
    echo Error: Unsupported Visual Studio version: %VS_MAJOR%
    echo Supported versions: VS2019 (16.x^), VS2022 (17.x^), VS2026 (18.x^)
    exit /b 1
)

echo Detected Visual Studio %VS_VERSION% (version %VS_MAJOR%)
echo Using CMake generator: %CMAKE_GENERATOR%

:generator_ready

@REM Pack deps
if "%1"=="pack" (
    setlocal ENABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION
    cd %WP%/deps/build
    if "%arch%"=="ARM64" cd %WP%/deps/build-arm64
    for /f "tokens=2-4 delims=/ " %%a in ('date /t') do set build_date=%%c%%b%%a
    echo packing deps: OrcaSlicer_dep_win-!arch!_!build_date!_vs!VS_VERSION!.zip

    %WP%/tools/7z.exe a OrcaSlicer_dep_win-!arch!_!build_date!_vs!VS_VERSION!.zip OrcaSlicer_dep
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    goto :done
)

set debug=OFF
set debuginfo=OFF
if "%1"=="debug" set debug=ON
if "%2"=="debug" set debug=ON
if "%1"=="debuginfo" set debuginfo=ON
if "%2"=="debuginfo" set debuginfo=ON
if "%debug%"=="ON" (
    set build_type=Debug
    set build_dir=build-dbg
) else (
    if "%debuginfo%"=="ON" (
        set build_type=RelWithDebInfo
        set build_dir=build-dbginfo
    ) else (
        set build_type=Release
        set build_dir=build
    )
)
if "%arch%"=="ARM64" set build_dir=%build_dir%-arm64
echo build type set to %build_type%, arch=%arch%

setlocal DISABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION
cd deps
mkdir %build_dir%
cd %build_dir%
set "SIG_FLAG="
if defined ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY set "SIG_FLAG=-DORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY=%ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY%"

if "%1"=="slicer" (
    GOTO :slicer
)
echo "building deps.."

echo on
REM Set minimum CMake policy to avoid <3.5 errors
set CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5
if "%USE_NINJA%"=="1" (
    cmake ../ -G %CMAKE_GENERATOR% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target deps
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
) else (
    cmake ../ -G %CMAKE_GENERATOR% -A %arch% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target deps -- -m
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
)
@echo off

if "%1"=="deps" goto :done

:slicer
echo "building Orca Slicer..."
cd %WP%
mkdir %build_dir%
cd %build_dir%

echo on
set CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5
if "%USE_NINJA%"=="1" (
    cmake .. -G %CMAKE_GENERATOR% -DORCA_TOOLS=ON %SIG_FLAG% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
) else (
    cmake .. -G %CMAKE_GENERATOR% -A %arch% -DORCA_TOOLS=ON %SIG_FLAG% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
)
@echo off
cd ..
call scripts/run_gettext.bat
if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
cd %build_dir%
cmake --build . --target install --config %build_type%
if errorlevel 1 goto :failed

:done
@echo off
for /f "tokens=1-3 delims=:.," %%a in ("%_START_TIME: =0%") do set /a "_start_s=%%a*3600+%%b*60+%%c"
for /f "tokens=1-3 delims=:.," %%a in ("%TIME: =0%") do set /a "_end_s=%%a*3600+%%b*60+%%c"
set /a "_elapsed=_end_s - _start_s"
if %_elapsed% lss 0 set /a "_elapsed+=86400"
set /a "_hours=_elapsed / 3600"
set /a "_remainder=_elapsed - _hours * 3600"
set /a "_mins=_remainder / 60"
set /a "_secs=_remainder - _mins * 60"
echo.
echo Build completed in %_hours%h %_mins%m %_secs%s
exit /b 0

@REM A build step failed. Exit with its code so callers and CI see the
@REM failure; ERRORLEVEL must be captured before echo resets it.
:failed
set "_rc=%ERRORLEVEL%"
if "%_rc%"=="0" set "_rc=1"
echo.
echo Build FAILED with exit code %_rc%
exit /b %_rc%

Tests are running. Here's the finding while they go:

## The commit you pulled doesn't compile on Windows

[tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp:1893](tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp:1893) and [:1907](tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp:1907) call `setenv`, which is POSIX — MSVC has no such function (`error C3861`). It builds on your Mac and dies here.

`setenv` is only the compile error. That one test case — *"mcp_connect runs an injected CLI runner"* — has three more POSIX assumptions that would still fail at **runtime** on Windows once it compiles:

| Line | Assumes | Windows needs |
|---|---|---|
| 1893 | `setenv(...)` | `_putenv_s` |
| 1892 | `":"` PATH separator | `';'` |
| 1888 | fixture named `claude` | `claude.exe` |

That list isn't guesswork — it's exactly what your own production code already does. [McpCatalog.cpp:52](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpCatalog.cpp:52) `command_on_path` branches on `_WIN32` to search for `command + ".exe"` split on `';'`. **The shipping code is portable; only the test is not.** So the test can't presently prove `command_on_path` works on the platform where its Windows branch actually runs.

There are no `#ifdef` guards anywhere in that file, so this is the sole compile blocker — every other suite built.

Two ways to go:

1. **Make the test portable** — a `_WIN32` branch mirroring `command_on_path`: `_putenv_s`, `';'`, and a `claude.exe` fixture. Small, and it makes the suite actually exercise the Windows path.
2. **Guard the test out on Windows** — smaller diff, but leaves `command_on_path`'s `_WIN32` branch untested on Windows, which is the branch most likely to break.

I'd go with (1); it's a few lines and buys real coverage. Want me to write it? I'll hold off touching your commit until you say.

Probe removed, tree clean, test binary rebuilding without it. Here's what I found.

## What's wrong

The MCP discovery file is a little file JusPrin writes so other programs can find it. The code updates it the careful way: write a new copy to a side file, then swap it into place in one move, so nobody ever sees a half-written file.

**On Windows that swap fails as soon as anything is reading the file.** Windows refuses with "Access is denied."

It's not a rare race. In my test it failed after a *single* read — basically the first instant a reader had the file open.

## How I know

The crash leaves a mess behind, and the mess tells the story: every crashed run left exactly one leftover side file, complete and correct at 251 bytes. So writing worked fine. Only the swap failed.

I then wrote a throwaway probe that caught the error instead of crashing, and it named it outright: `Publish MCP discovery: Access is denied.` I've since deleted the probe.

## Why it crashes so violently

When the swap fails, the code raises an error. The test that was running had a background thread going at the time, and that thread was never shut down before the error escaped. Windows responds by killing the whole process instantly — no message, no failure report, just a hard exit. That's why the test output was blank.

That part is the test's fault. The failed swap underneath it is not.

## What this means for the real app

The same function runs at JusPrin startup — it's called while constructing `McpRuntime`, in the member initializer list, which is the worst possible spot: if it throws there, the object never finishes building.

I want to be straight about the limits of what I've shown. I proved the swap fails **when another reader has the file open**. At startup, on a normal machine, usually nothing else is reading it yet, which is likely why this has never bitten you. The realistic triggers are a second JusPrin running, an editor or antivirus touching the file, or a client polling it. I have not tested those, so I can't tell you how often it happens in practice.

What I can say is that the design's central promise — that this update is safe while others are reading — does not hold on Windows.

## Worth knowing

The rest of that code is genuinely well built for Windows. Readers already open the file in the special mode that's *supposed* to permit exactly this kind of swap, and the swap uses the right Windows call. Somebody thought about this carefully. The chosen call just doesn't behave the way it looks like it should. Windows has a different function meant for replacing files that are currently open, which is likely the fix.

Two things I have **not** done: fixed this, or touched the separate PlaceholderParser crash you told me to skip. Say the word if you want the fix.

cd C:/src/JusPrin; git commit -F - <<'EOF'
Publish MCP discovery without breaking on open readers

Replacing the discovery record used MoveFileExW, which fails with
ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED the moment any process holds the target open. Readers
hold it open constantly by design, so the publish did not merely race --
it failed almost immediately, after a single read in a loop of fifty
writes. Sharing delete access does not rescue the ordinary rename, and
the write_discovery contract of a reader never seeing a partial record
could not be honoured on Windows at all.

FileRenameInfoEx with POSIX semantics is the rename that behaves like
rename(2): the name is rebound at once while existing handles keep
reading the file they already opened. It needs NTFS and Windows 10 1607,
so a volume that cannot do it falls back to the previous replace rather
than refusing to publish, leaving those cases no worse than before.

The failure was invisible until now because agent_bridge_tests did not
compile on Windows. Once it did, the atomicity test took the process
down with it: write_discovery threw, the throw escaped a scope holding a
joinable reader thread, and the std::thread destructor called
std::terminate. Windows reports that as a bare 0xC0000409 fast-fail with
no Catch2 output, which is why a real defect looked like a crashing test.
That fragility is left alone here; it stops mattering once the publish
succeeds.

Verified on Windows: the atomicity test passed fifteen consecutive runs
having previously failed every one, and ctest reports one failure out of
414, the pre-existing PlaceholderParser segfault this does not touch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
